title: Starbucks Reserve
description: Created with the Starbucks Asia Pacific team in Hong Kong for the Reserve store at SM North Towers, these three layered-MDF sculptures trace the origins of coffee through wildlife. A Sumatran tiger, Kenyan elephant, and Guatemalan quetzal translate their regions into pattern, texture, and relief.
context: The installation carries Patrick’s paper-cutting language into a larger and more durable material. The tiger measures 110 × 110 × 20 cm; Patrick and Camy spent almost two months sanding, priming, painting, and airbrushing it. The Kenyan elephant measures 110 × 150 cm, while the quetzal represents Guatemala. Patrick’s brother Ian helped with mounting. Together, the sculptures show how a familiar studio process changes at architectural scale, with surface preparation and finishing becoming as important as the layered design.
sources: The Starbucks Reserve commission · adobo magazine

captions.74: Patrick Cabral with the Starbucks Reserve collection

title: Mananayaw ng Langit at Lupa
description: Dancers of Heaven and Earth: two masks made from archival coloured paper for the Dinagyang Festival in 2021. The blue bird, Langit, evokes air, flight, horizons, and dreams. The red and yellow dragon or buwaya, Lupa, brings together fire, earth, light, and passion.
alt: Mananayaw ng Langit at Lupa, paired blue and red masks made from archival coloured paper
context: Commissioned by Edwin Valencia for the Iloilo Museum of Contemporary Art, the work is recorded at 32 × 38 inches. The paired figures explore duality through colour, movement, and layers of ornament. Their imagery draws together faith, trade, and worship, giving each mask a distinct character while allowing them to form a single conversation between the earthly and the celestial.

title: Roosters in Colour
description: Roosters meet in expansive compositions of colour and movement. Layered feathers spread into rhythmic fans, with blue, red, gold, and violet turning their charged encounter into intricate sculptural silhouettes.
alt: Colourful layered-paper rooster compositions with wide-spreading wings and intricate feathers
context: The landscape composition measures six by four feet and began as a self-initiated work. Patrick devoted about one working day each week to it over roughly a year. The limited range of coloured paper available shaped the palette, making colour selection part of the challenge alongside the scale and complexity of the layered feathers. The gallery also includes a separate portrait composition.

captions.17: Landscape composition · 6 × 4 feet, developed over roughly a year
captions.46: Portrait composition · layered feathers and colour

title: Parol
description: A familiar Filipino symbol becomes an elaborate study in symmetry. Jewel-like colour and repeated patterns radiate outward from a central star.

title: Parol II
description: A second exploration of the star-shaped Filipino lantern. Concentric layers of blue, yellow, pink, and green gather around the centre, creating depth through colour and repetition.

title: Fudog
description: An expressive guardian face, built from vivid interlocking shapes. Curls, flames, and repeating contours create a dense surface of sculptural ornament.

title: Roosters in White
description: An encounter suspended in motion. Two birds rise through a composition of outstretched wings and cascading tails, each feather articulated through delicate layers and repeating patterns.
alt: Roosters in White by Patrick Cabral

title: Crowned Lion
description: A regal feline portrait framed by an elaborate mane and crown. Fine ornamental contours give the white and gold layers a lace-like delicacy.

title: Elephant
description: A frontal elephant portrait shaped by patterned layers. Wide ears, curled tusks, and a sweeping trunk turn an instantly recognisable animal into an intricate arrangement of curves.

title: Tiger
description: A tiger portrait articulated through delicate white layers and dark outlines. The close views reveal how repeated patterns give structure to the cheeks, brows, and muzzle.

title: Tiger in Blue
description: A tiger portrait commissioned by Mentorque, with white layered features set against a radiating blue silhouette. Blue lines follow the face’s contours, bringing colour into the dense ornament around its eyes, cheeks, and muzzle.
alt: White tiger portrait with blue ornamental details and a radiating blue perimeter
context: This commission was Patrick’s first blue tiger. The result surprised him: the unfamiliar colour worked well with the layered construction, giving the portrait a new character while retaining the symmetry and fine detail of his animal work.

title: Tiger in Gold
description: A white tiger portrait traced with fine gold contours. Repeating arches follow the face and build a layered relief around its eyes and muzzle.
alt: Tiger in Gold by Patrick Cabral

title: Lion
description: An expressive lion portrait framed by a mane of overlapping, petal-like forms. An installation photograph places the layered sculpture in its architectural setting.

title: Lion / Openwork
description: Open contours and pointed shapes form a sweeping mane. This lion explores the contrast between a solid face and the delicate outer silhouette of its ornament.

title: Rhinoceros in White
description: A sculptural rhinoceros with a surface of repeated, lace-like detail. White layers follow the full body, bringing delicate patterns to a powerful animal silhouette.
alt: Rhinoceros in White by Patrick Cabral

title: Dhole
description: An alert wild-dog portrait rendered in fine white layers. A dense field of cut detail follows the face while the ears establish a crisp, recognisable outline.

title: Gorilla
description: A quiet portrait with a richly patterned surface. Overlapping layers define the brow, muzzle, and outline of a gorilla’s face.

title: Iberian Lynx
description: Tufted ears and a long facial silhouette become a framework for layered ornament. Curving motifs move across the face, drawing attention toward the eyes.

title: Tamaraw
description: The curved horns and broad face of a tamaraw become a symmetrical layered portrait. Fine patterns gather around the eyes and flow outward across its silhouette.

title: Hippopotamus
description: A broad, rounded animal portrait built from repeated contours. Gold accents and fine white patterning bring rhythm to the face.

title: Dog Portrait
description: A white dog portrait with soft, floppy ears and an intricately patterned face. A small collar tag brings a personal detail to the layered composition.

title: Cat
description: A cat’s face emerges from intricately layered white ornament. Clear eyes and pointed ears anchor a surface of delicate repeating motifs.

title: British Shorthair Cat
description: A British Shorthair cat rendered in intricately layered blue-grey paper. Golden eyes and rounded cheeks give the seated figure its character, while delicate repeating patterns trace the body and curled tail.
alt: Layered blue-grey paper sculpture of a British Shorthair cat with golden eyes by Patrick Cabral
content_source: Subject identified by Patrick Cabral as a British Shorthair cat, 14 November 2026.

title: Bee
description: An insect becomes a sculptural study in symmetry. Delicate open wings extend from a richly patterned body, revealing the relationship between structure and ornament.

title: Eagle
description: An eagle held in a moment of movement, with lifted wings and sharply defined feathers. Layers of white detail give the silhouette both volume and delicacy.

title: Penguin Books
description: Commissioned by Paul Buckley for Penguin Books’ New York headquarters, a white penguin sits within a deep field of warm, stepped colour. The project connects Patrick’s paper practice with a publisher whose books helped shape his curiosity as a child.
alt: White layered-paper penguin against a stepped red and amber background, commissioned for Penguin Books
context: Patrick had long admired Buckley’s work, including his collaborations with Alex Trochut. The commission also brought back memories of a childhood Random House encyclopedia, through which Patrick encountered subjects such as Albrecht Dürer and Frank Lloyd Wright’s Fallingwater. Finding the right background was a separate challenge: Patrick and Camy repeatedly repainted its layers, mixing a difficult gradient until the colours gave the white figure enough contrast. Shared in July 2019, the piece records both a personal connection to books and the patient work behind its apparently simple colour transitions.

title: Philippine Cockatoo
description: A Philippine cockatoo perched on a branch, its raised crest and curved beak framed by fine layers of feather-like ornament. The pale construction brings out the changing rhythms of the wings, chest, and long tail.
alt: Pale layered Philippine cockatoo with a raised crest, perched on a branch
context: The second of a three-bird commission, this work depicts a species endemic to the Philippines. Together with the Palawan peacock-pheasant and Palawan hornbill, it forms a collection devoted to the country’s wildlife, translating each bird’s character into a distinct sculptural profile.

title: Horses
description: Two white horses stretch through a flowing, horizontal composition. Layered surface detail follows their bodies, balancing movement with intricate repetition.

title: Shark
description: A four-foot-wide shark made for a commission in Hong Kong. Its long, pale body stretches across a dark framed background, with overlapping patterns giving the fins and flanks a sense of movement.
alt: Four-foot-wide pale shark relief in a dark horizontal frame, commissioned for Hong Kong
context: The streamlined silhouette required repeated revisions. Patrick’s project notes record the head at roughly its fourth version, showing how much adjustment sits behind a form that reads immediately as a shark. The finished relief brings that recognisable outline together with intricate surface detail.

title: Pangolin
description: A curled animal figure forms an almost circular composition. Its repeated scale-like layers make texture the central structure of the work.

title: White & Gold Dragon
description: A long white dragon moves across a horizontal composition. Gold details accent the curling body, horns, and limbs, drawing the eye along its patterned surface.
alt: White & Gold Dragon by Patrick Cabral

title: Intertwined Dragons
description: Two dragons weave through a single expansive composition. Their curving bodies and fine surface patterns create a conversation between movement and balance.

title: Dragon & Serpent
description: A dragon and a serpent face one another in a curling composition. White and gold layers articulate their bodies and give shape to the space between them.

title: Dragon & Fish
description: A pale dragon and surrounding fish move over a warm gold ground. Interwoven silhouettes form a flowing composition of water, motion, and ornament.

title: Golden Dragon
description: A six-foot-wide golden dragon built from approximately two hundred layers of gold PVC sheets. Its long body rises and falls in sweeping curves, with closely repeated scales leading into finely articulated claws, whiskers, and horns.
alt: Six-foot-wide golden dragon made from approximately two hundred layers of gold PVC sheets
context: Patrick began this work in November 2017 and shared it in 2018. The gold PVC gives the dragon a material character distinct from his paper sculptures, while the repeated layers retain the same attention to depth and fine detail. A dark background makes the full length of its winding silhouette visible.

title: Winged Figures
description: Two winged figures meet in a cloud-like arrangement of curves. Layered surfaces give shape to the bodies, feathers, and surrounding relief.

title: Honkai Impact 3rd
description: A commissioned artwork for Honkai Impact 3rd’s fourth-anniversary giveaway, this figure translates a game character into approximately fifty layers of paper. White hair, armour, a sword, and a sweeping red cape bring the character’s movement into a dimensional composition.
alt: White-haired Honkai Impact 3rd character with a sword and red cape, built from approximately fifty paper layers
context: This was Patrick’s first full-bodied human figure in layered paper, extending a practice previously centred on animals and ornamental forms. The commission also had a personal connection: the character was a favourite of his niece. Patrick recorded the making process, showing how many separate paper layers come together to create the pose, costume, and depth of the finished work.

title: Our Lady of Peñafrancia
description: A layered paper interpretation of Our Lady of Peñafrancia, affectionately called Ina. Created for Patrick’s friends Sweet and Joseph, the piece celebrates a milestone in their lives while holding close the faith, friendships, and sense of home that shaped them.
alt: Our Lady of Peñafrancia with the Child Jesus, depicted in ornate layered paper with a radiating halo
context: Patrick and Joseph’s friendship reaches back to childhood, when they served together as altar boys. They later shared a home while studying in Naga City, and again when they began working in Manila. Delivered to Joseph and Sweet as they built their life in Dallas, the sculpture became a reminder of where they came from. When it was unpacked, several of those present were also devotees of Ina, turning the occasion into an unexpected moment of shared devotion.
sources: The story of Sweet, Joseph, and Ina · Instagram
content_source: Artwork identity confirmed by Patrick Cabral; story cross-checked against his Instagram caption

title: Our Lady of Manaoag
description: A layered paper interpretation of Our Lady of Manaoag, holding the Child Jesus beneath an ornate golden crown and halo. Deep blue, plum, and gold frame the figures, while curling foliage and a layered flower surround them with intricate ornament.
context: Lace-like cutwork runs through the robes, halo, and foliage. Stacked paper creates depth through real edges and shadows, with details extending from the faces and crowns to the rosary and the flower at the base of the composition.
alt: Our Lady of Manaoag holding the Child Jesus, a layered paper sculpture in blue, plum, green, and gold by Patrick Cabral
content_source: Artist-supplied Manaoag project folder, 14 November 2026. Description based on the four supplied artwork photographs.

title: Dragon & Koi
description: A dragon and fish weave through an intricate square composition. White and gold layers intertwine against a dark ground.

title: Royal Mint · Money Heist
description: Created with Netflix Philippines for Money Heist, this paper interpretation of the Royal Mint of Spain turns a symbol of institutional power into something delicate. Its white façade is built from intricate layers, with ornamental detail inspired by the engraved lines of banknotes.
alt: The Royal Mint of Spain rendered in white layered paper for Netflix Philippines and Money Heist
context: Patrick chose the Royal Mint rather than the series’ familiar Dalí mask because architecture offered a new challenge. The building represents the system at the heart of the story; rendering it in fragile paper creates a tension between authority and vulnerability. Published in September 2021, the project brings the precision of architectural relief together with the visual language of currency. Detail views reveal the columns, windows, and decorative edges that give the façade its depth.

title: Darth Vader
description: An iconic dark helmet translated into layered ornament. Fine surface detail follows its familiar curves and angular contours.

title: Cha Long Wolves
description: Commissioned by Maxim’s Hong Kong for its Cha Long brand, these wolf characters are built from laser-cut plywood. Layered faces, expressive clothing, and carefully painted details turn the brand’s characters into dimensional portraits.
alt: Cha Long wolf character assembled from laser-cut, painted plywood layers
context: The project adapts the visual language of Patrick’s paper work to wood. Patrick handled sanding while Camy painted the layers, a division of work that brought the complex construction and colour together. The second wolf’s hat alone used roughly twenty colours. The finished characters combine the precision of laser cutting with the patient surface work required to give each painted layer its own presence.

title: Ornamental Creature
description: A seated fantastical creature with a curled tail and highly patterned surface. Sweeping contours and delicate ornament give the compact sculpture an expressive silhouette.

title: Baboon with Bitcoin
description: A commissioned baboon holding a Bitcoin coin, inspired by the Egyptian deity Thoth. A warm red face sits within a broad metallic mane, while patterned hands, arms, and legs gather around the gold coin at its centre.
alt: Metallic-paper baboon with a red face holding a gold Bitcoin coin
context: Made for a patron to celebrate cryptocurrency and Bitcoin, this was Patrick’s first work created entirely from metallic paper. The commission brings an ancient source of imagery into conversation with a contemporary symbol, using the reflective material to distinguish the face, fur, and coin.

title: Lettering in Relief
description: Bold lettering surrounded by a dense arrangement of botanical ornament. White layers and deep shadows set the directness of the word against the delicacy of its sculptural setting.
alt: Ornamental white layered sculpture spelling FUCK by Patrick Cabral

title: White Lettering
description: A typographic composition built from close-set white layers. Letterforms sit within a field of repeated contours, creating a quiet interplay of language and relief.

title: Calligraphic Monogram
description: A flowing monogram rendered in vivid turquoise and green. Sweeping letterforms bring the movement of calligraphy into a dimensional composition.

title: Faceted Vessel
description: A vessel study shaped by closely stacked contours and a faceted opening. Alternate views reveal the changing rhythm of the rim and outer surface.

title: Lattice Form
description: An open ovoid structure with a metallic finish. Interconnected cells define a form through its empty spaces as much as through its surface.

title: Organic Forms
description: Flowing white forms with deep openings and layered surface rhythms. Seen from multiple angles, the continuous outer shell breaks into folds, channels, and porous spaces.
context: The Bone image sequence in the Techsugi archive records the form through changing viewpoints. These selected views extend the original two studies, revealing how the openings and overlapping surfaces change around the object.

title: Philippine Basketry · Fiber
description: An algorithmic study inspired by Philippine basketry. Given a three-dimensional silhouette, the system generates an intricate woven structure that follows its form. In Fiber, fine coloured strands trace the folds and openings of an ovoid surface.
alt: Fine coloured strands following the folds of an ovoid form in Philippine Basketry · Fiber
context: The experiment translates the structural logic of basketry into a flexible digital process. Full views and close details reveal how many individual paths describe the same continuous form. The method can also extend to moving forms.

captions.104: Philippine Basketry · Fiber flowing colour detail

title: Branching Tree
description: A digital study of branching structure. Fine lines accumulate into a tree-like form, exploring growth through repeated divisions.

title: Branching Figure
description: The human silhouette interpreted as a network of fine branching paths. Full figures and a closer view explore the relationship between organic growth and a recognisable body.
context: The Techsugi archive brings together delicate line figures and a warm-toned detail of a head and shoulders. The close view reveals how the branching structure fills the silhouette while leaving its interior open.

captions.106: Branching figure · head and shoulder detail

title: Twisting Forms
description: A pair of twisting forms built from stacked ribs. Repeated elements create fluid silhouettes that change in density and direction.

title: Tower Studies
description: An award concept built around the letter T in a client’s logo. Stacked, shifting profiles turn the letter into two slender skyscraper forms, exploring how a graphic identity might become a sculptural object.
alt: Two digital trophy concepts shaped as slender towers derived from the letter T
context: The original request was for a certificate; Patrick proposed a trophy instead. Paper was the intended material, but the images document the design study rather than a manufactured award. The concept uses repetition and changing outlines to move between a recognisable letter, an architectural silhouette, and an object that could mark an achievement.

title: Chair Studies
description: Two chairs explored as continuous, sculptural gestures. Looping profiles blur the boundary between furniture and expressive line.

title: Topographical Beads
description: Philippine landscapes translated into digital beadwork. Geographical contours and elevation lines become thousands of densely arranged, coloured spheres, giving the shape of the land a tactile, patterned presence.
alt: Topographical Beads by Patrick Cabral, coloured digital spheres arranged in layered geographical contours
context: The work connects cartography with the careful repetition of traditional beadwork. The landscape becomes a crafted surface, inviting the viewer to read its ridges, valleys, and changing elevations through colour and detail.

captions.22: Topographical Beads · contours in digital beadwork

title: Chromatic Mask
description: A mask-like face formed from vivid geometric marks against a dark ground. Dense colour and rhythmic line create a distinctly graphic portrait.

title: Paired Eagles
description: Two eagles face one another with wings lifted. Fine patterned feathers create a mirrored composition, balancing the birds with the open space between them.

title: Rhinoceros in Gold
description: A warm gold-toned rhinoceros with an elaborately patterned surface. Repeated contours follow the animal’s body, tracing the broad silhouette and distinctive horns.
alt: Rhinoceros in Gold by Patrick Cabral

title: Palawan Peacock-Pheasant
description: A Palawan peacock-pheasant, a species endemic to the Philippines, rendered in intricate pale layers. Its upright crest, folded wings, and broad trailing tail turn the bird’s distinctive silhouette into a study of feather patterns and depth.
alt: Palawan peacock-pheasant with a tall crest and long layered tail in pale sculpted feathers
context: The first of three birds made for the same client, this work begins a commission celebrating Philippine wildlife. The series also includes the Philippine cockatoo and Palawan hornbill. Its focus on native species connects the patient work of making with a concern for environmental sustainability.

title: Palawan Hornbill
description: The Palawan hornbill’s curved beak and prominent casque give this perched bird its unmistakable profile. Fine layered detail runs from the head through the folded wings to the long tail, giving a pale silhouette depth and texture.
alt: Pale layered Palawan hornbill perched on a branch, with a prominent casque and long tail
context: This is the final bird in a three-piece commission featuring species endemic to the Philippines. Made for the same client as the Palawan peacock-pheasant and Philippine cockatoo, it completes a collection shaped by the variety of the country’s native wildlife.

title: Stormtrooper
description: A familiar white science-fiction helmet interpreted through delicate sculptural pattern. The contrast between light and dark preserves the character of its iconic silhouette.

title: Philippine Basketry · Woven Form
description: Philippine basketry translated into a procedural structure. The algorithm accepts a three-dimensional silhouette and generates a complex woven surface, allowing the underlying form to guide the arrangement of its details.
alt: A warm-toned ovoid with interlocking woven structures in Philippine Basketry · Woven Form
context: This warm-toned study explores density, depth, and the spaces between interlocking elements. Part of the Philippine Basketry experiments, the same approach can extend from still objects to moving forms.

title: Geometric Lion
description: A lion-like face built from interlocking, stepped planes. Bright colour separates the angular pieces, while a monochrome version brings the structure and depth of the relief into focus.
context: Full views, a close detail, and a three-version comparison from the Techsugi archive show how colour and surface treatment change the same geometric language.
alt: A geometric lion-like face with interlocking stepped surfaces by Patrick Cabral

title: Kalinga Tattoo Patterns
description: An algorithmic study inspired by the pattern language of traditional Kalinga tattooing. Repetition, rhythm, and placement become starting points for a contemporary interpretation through code.
context: Applied to digital figures, the generated patterns follow the contours of the body. The study explores the relationship between a patterned surface and the form it inhabits.
alt: Digital figures covered in algorithmic patterns inspired by traditional Kalinga tattooing

captions.112: Kalinga Tattoo Patterns · gold surface study
captions.111: Kalinga Tattoo Patterns · dark surface study
captions.113: Kalinga Tattoo Patterns · monochrome figure study

title: Textile Physics
description: An experiment in making digital textiles easier to art-direct, from the shape of a fold to the way a surface moves. Fabric becomes a material for choreography, guided as deliberately as a sculptor shapes a surface.
context: The accompanying film, Quantum Dance, demonstrates a Houdini system that develops fabric-like forms from an edge or path. Noise remapping drives the motion, while curvature controls the appearance of creases. The study explores how an artist can guide textile form and behaviour with greater control.
alt: Quantum Dance, a demonstration of Patrick Cabral’s Textile Physics experiment

captions.121: Textile Physics · a frame from Quantum Dance

title: Modern Patterns
description: An evolution of Patrick’s earlier weaving experiments, Modern Patterns reimagines textile structures through the geometry of Manhattan Voronoi. Interlocking shapes draw on the visual language of science fiction, skyscrapers, and circuit boards.
context: The work is inspired by the T’boli Dreamweavers and the stories carried through their textiles. Growing up alongside rapid technological change, Patrick draws from the images and structures of his own era to explore how a personal story might take the form of a pattern.
alt: Interlocking geometric surfaces from Modern Patterns by Patrick Cabral

captions.126: Modern Patterns · Version 2, an image translated through the digital loom

study_sections.title: Version 2 · A digital loom
study_sections.description: The second version uses dynamic tessellation to translate an image or video into an intricate pattern in real time. Acting as a digital loom, the system continually rebuilds its structure in response to the incoming imagery. This still demonstrates the process through a reinterpretation of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

title: Generative Footwear
description: A sculptural shoe built from clustered geometric volumes. Colour separates the growing forms as they wrap around the upper and extend into a segmented sole.
context: Created with a custom three-dimensional Manhattan Voronoi generator in Houdini. Patrick developed the workflow while exploring generative fashion, replacing the repeated resculpting that changes to 3D-printing designs had required in ZBrush with a more adaptable procedural approach.
alt: A digital shoe with colourful segmented volumes by Patrick Cabral

title: Grown
description: A digital garment imagined as something that grows around the body. Inspired by the intricate pathways of mycelial networks, its details gather into a silhouette with the character of a living organism.
context: Growth becomes a way of thinking about structure. The study explores how individual forms can spread, connect, and accumulate around a figure, creating a garment that appears to have bloomed into shape.
alt: A digital garment of colourful organic forms growing around a figure in Grown

captions.116: Grown · a garment imagined through organic growth

title: Digital Armour
description: Dark fitted armour and a segmented head explore the boundary between a body and a constructed surface. Reflective plates, narrow seams, and accents of light give the figures a mechanical character.
context: The Robo head demonstrates a sci-fi panel generator built in Houdini to simplify hard-surface modelling, with clean topology intended for use in games. Patrick cited MGXS as an inspiration for this experiment. It appears here alongside a separate fitted-armour study from the Techsugi archive.
sources: Artist’s Robo and panel-generator notes · Instagram

title: Cypher
description: An algorithmic tool that automatically arranges and resizes text into dynamic layouts. Its letterforms adapt fluidly while preserving the continuity of their curves.
context: Originally developed to conceal messages within symbolic art, Cypher explores how language can become a changing visual structure. A version for Baybayin is currently in development, extending this research into a different writing system.
alt: Fluid letterforms arranged into a dense dynamic layout by Cypher

title: Philippine Weave AR
description: An augmented reality experiment that transforms live video into patterns inspired by traditional Philippine weaving. As people move in front of the camera, their presence becomes part of a continuously changing digital textile.
context: The audience becomes an active part of the artwork. Faces, gestures, and movement become threads, bringing the people in the room into a shared, unfolding interpretation of Philippine culture.
alt: A moving figure translated into coloured woven patterns in Philippine Weave AR

captions.122: Philippine Weave AR · a figure woven into the pattern

title: Rosa
description: Bright ribbons open and fold into a flower-like form. The shifting surfaces move between petal, fabric, and abstract sculpture.
context: Named Rosa in the Techsugi archive, the motion study uses contrasting colour to make each curling surface legible as the form changes. The dark background isolates the changing silhouette.
